bug_description.normalized: In vulnerable commit `ab99479c96ba9759193b3b1f42089e5fe1b647f6`, YARA's .NET metadata parser reads the attacker-controlled AssemblyRef row count from the `#~` stream and iterates that many times in `dotnet_parse_tilde_2()`. The loop initializes `row_ptr` to the first AssemblyRef row, but its per-iteration bounds check tests `fits_in_pe(pe, table_offset, row_size)` instead of the advancing cursor `row_ptr`. Because `table_offset` stays fixed at the first row, an input where that initial row fits but the declared row count exceeds the number of complete AssemblyRef rows remaining from that pointer can drive later iterations after `row_ptr` has advanced past the mapped PE image. A later iteration then reads `assemblyref_table->RevisionNumber` through that invalid pointer, and the staged MemorySanitizer trace reports `SEGV` caused by a READ at `libyara/modules/dotnet.c:1152` in `dotnet_parse_tilde_2`. Commit `72c109ea85f1434237a292de3478f53554989453` fixes the bug by checking `row_ptr` instead of `table_offset`.

source.description: On the crashing path, the second `#~`-table walk reads the attacker-controlled row count for the current table into `num_rows`. When `bit_check` reaches `BIT_ASSEMBLYREF`, this value becomes the number of AssemblyRef rows the vulnerable loop will try to parse.
source.value_from: The staged 4892-byte `poc` is a PE/.NET image whose `#~` metadata stream supplies the row-count array immediately after `tilde_header`. `row_offset + matched_bits` selects the attacker-controlled slot for the current table; on the crashing path that slot is the AssemblyRef count.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer's crashing read happens when a later AssemblyRef iteration dereferences `assemblyref_table->RevisionNumber`. By then `assemblyref_table` aliases an out-of-bounds `row_ptr`, so this field read triggers the observed `SEGV on unknown address` caused by a READ.

root_cause.description: The AssemblyRef loop revalidates the fixed table start `table_offset` instead of the advancing row cursor `row_ptr`. Once the first row fits, this check stays satisfied on later iterations even after `row_ptr` has moved past the mapped PE data. The fix changes the check to `fits_in_pe(pe, row_ptr, row_size)`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant attacker-controlled value is the AssemblyRef row count loaded from the `#~` metadata rows array into `num_rows`. That count later controls how many times the loop can advance `row_ptr`.

parser_admitted.code: if (headers.tilde != NULL && headers.string != NULL && headers.blob != NULL) dotnet_parse_tilde(pe, metadata_root, cli_header, &headers);
parser_admitted.description: The vulnerable path is only entered after stream-header parsing finds non-NULL `#~`, `#Strings`, and `#Blob` streams and `dotnet_parse_com()` dispatches into `dotnet_parse_tilde()`. The staged crash stack confirms `dotnet_parse_tilde_2 -> dotnet_parse_tilde -> dotnet_parse_com`.

coarse_trace.summary: After the PE/.NET headers and stream headers are accepted, `dotnet_parse_com()` calls `dotnet_parse_tilde()` to walk the attacker-controlled `#~` metadata tables.

In the `BIT_ASSEMBLYREF` case, `dotnet_parse_tilde_2()` uses the attacker-controlled AssemblyRef row count as the loop bound and initializes `row_ptr` to the first AssemblyRef row, which must fit once at `table_offset` for the loop body to start.

The AssemblyRef loop checks `table_offset` instead of `row_ptr`, so inputs with one in-bounds initial row but too-large `num_rows` let later iterations advance beyond the PE mapping and then read `assemblyref_table->RevisionNumber` through the invalid row pointer, producing the observed MSan crash.

fine_trace.note: When the second metadata-table walk reaches the AssemblyRef table, it loads the attacker-controlled row-count entry from the `#~` rows array into `num_rows`. This is the value that later determines how many AssemblyRef rows the parser believes exist.

In the AssemblyRef case, the parser computes the byte width of one row, seeds the live cursor `row_ptr` with the first AssemblyRef row at `table_offset`, and uses attacker-controlled `num_rows` as the loop bound. That setup means each iteration should validate the current `row_ptr` before dereferencing row fields.

Root cause. The per-iteration guard rechecks only the fixed table start `table_offset`, not the advancing `row_ptr`. After the initial AssemblyRef row fits, later iterations still stay in the loop body while `i < num_rows` even when the current cursor has already moved beyond the mapped PE bytes.

Any AssemblyRef iteration that does not break at step 3 advances `row_ptr` by one row before the next loop test. The vulnerable source performs the same `row_ptr += row_size;` at line 1169 on the blob-failure `continue` path and again at line 1197 on the normal path, so successive iterations can keep moving the live cursor past the PE mapping while the stale guard still revalidates only `table_offset`.

depends_on.via: break is not taken because `fits_in_pe(pe, table_offset, row_size)` still passes

fine_trace.note: MSan sink. On a later iteration, `assemblyref_table = (PASSEMBLYREF_TABLE) row_ptr` aliases the out-of-bounds cursor produced by repeated step-4 advances, and the read of `assemblyref_table->RevisionNumber` faults. The staged sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: SEGV on unknown address` caused by a READ at this line.

format.name: PE/.NET binary
format.contract: The staged 4892-byte witness is a PE/.NET binary that reaches `dotnet_parse_com()` with non-NULL `#~`, `#Strings`, and `#Blob` streams, marks the AssemblyRef table present, places at least one full AssemblyRef row at the initial `table_offset`, and declares an AssemblyRef `num_rows` larger than the number of complete AssemblyRef rows remaining from that starting pointer. That exact mismatch lets later iterations advance `row_ptr` past the PE bounds while the stale `fits_in_pe(pe, table_offset, row_size)` check still passes.
